config.title: Build a star rating component

intro.title: Build a star rating component
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a star rating component that allows users to select and display a rating from 1 to 5 stars. You will learn how to use JavaScript to manage state, handle user interactions, and dynamically update the UI based on user input. The main technologies involved are JavaScript functions, event listeners, and DOM manipulation to create an interactive experience. By the end, you will have a functional, reusable component that visually reflects the selected rating.
intro.usecase: Star rating components are a fundamental UI pattern for collecting and displaying user feedback. You'll see them in e-commerce product pages, app store reviews, and service platforms like Airbnb or Uber, where users rate their experience. As a developer, you'll build these interactive elements to enhance user engagement and gather valuable data for product improvement. Mastering this component teaches you how to handle user input, update UI state dynamically, and create reusable, accessible interface elements.

objectives: Construct a reusable star rating component with interactive UI elements
Implement state management to track the current and hovered rating values
Apply conditional rendering logic to display filled and empty stars based on rating
Bind event handlers to mouse interactions for dynamic rating selection
Configure the component to accept and display an initial rating value
Manipulate DOM elements to reflect user interactions in real-time
Initialize component properties and state for proper functionality

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from the 'react' library.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported, making them available for use in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: import both React and the useState hook from the 'react' library using the import statement.

steps.title: Create the StarRating component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named StarRating that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called StarRating that returns null. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the StarRating component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A StarRating component function is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: The code defines a StarRating component that returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined a component named StarRating that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a function called StarRating that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize rating state
steps.instruction: Inside the StarRating component, declare a state variable named 'rating' with an initial value of 0 using the useState hook.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Call it with 0 as the initial value, and destructure the returned array into 'rating' and 'setRating'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state variable with initial value
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a state variable 'rating' initialized to 0, ready to track the current star rating.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with 0, and the returned array is destructured into 'rating' and 'setRating'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with 0 as the initial value and destructuring the array into 'rating' and 'setRating'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the component, use useState(0) to create a state variable named 'rating'.

steps.title: Create handleMouseEnter function
steps.instruction: Inside your StarRating component, create a function named handleMouseEnter that takes a star index parameter and updates the hover state using the setHover function.
steps.hint: Define a function that receives a star index and calls setHover with that index.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a handleMouseEnter function that updates the hover state when called with a star index.
successCriteria: The handleMouseEnter function is defined, takes a star index parameter, and calls setHover with that index.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function takes a star index parameter and calls setHover with that index.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function should be named handleMouseEnter, take a star index parameter, and update the hover state using setHover.

steps.title: Return container div
steps.instruction: Return a div element from your StarRating component to serve as the container for the star rating UI.
steps.hint:
Replace the current return statement with a div element. You can use JSX syntax: return
;
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div container element instead of null.
successCriteria: The StarRating component returns a div element using JSX syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a div element using JSX syntax (with angle brackets).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div element. Check that you're using JSX syntax with angle brackets.

steps.title: Add star buttons with event handlers
steps.instruction: Inside the container div, create 5 button elements with onClick, onMouseEnter, and onMouseLeave handlers wired to the corresponding functions.
steps.hint: Use a loop or manually create 5 button elements. Each button should have onClick={handleClick}, onMouseEnter={handleMouseEnter}, and onMouseLeave={handleMouseLeave}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a container div with 5 button elements, each with onClick, onMouseEnter, and onMouseLeave handlers attached.
successCriteria: Five button elements are created inside the container div, each with onClick, onMouseEnter, and onMouseLeave handlers wired to the corresponding functions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some buttons, but make sure you have exactly 5 buttons and all three event handlers (onClick, onMouseEnter, onMouseLeave) are attached to each.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons aren't properly set up. Check that you have 5 button elements inside the container div, each with onClick, onMouseEnter, and onMouseLeave handlers.

steps.title: Add star display logic
steps.instruction: Inside the star buttons, add conditional logic to display filled stars when the star index is less than or equal to the current hover or rating state.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator to conditionally render a filled star character (★) or an empty star character (☆) based on whether the index is less than or equal to the hover state (if hover > 0) or the rating state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The star buttons will visually change between filled and empty states based on mouse hover and click interactions.
successCriteria: Each star button displays a filled star (★) when its index is less than or equal to the hover state (if hover > 0) or the rating state, otherwise displays an empty star (☆).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your conditional logic correctly uses both hover and rating states to determine which stars should be filled.
steps.feedbackWrong: The star display logic isn't working as expected. Make sure you're using a ternary operator to conditionally render the correct star character based on the current state values.
